Lumen 176.resource_aggregation: For each trial and metric, take the median of that trial's available one-second samples. The headline value is the median of those seven trial medians. Minimum and maximum are the extrema of all observed samples for that browser. This is not a median of per-trial maxima.
Lumen 176.resource_units: Decimal MB (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes); CPU percent is the sampled browser process-tree value.
Lumen 176.resource_scope: Fresh browser process tree over startup, workload and cleanup. Not steady idle, whole-system memory, or a phase-specific CPU measurement. Summed RSS can count shared mappings multiple times; PSS is sampled proportional memory.

performance_final.conclusion: All fixed-workload correctness checks and cleanup gates passed. The before/after Lumen timing ranges overlap and pair directions are mixed; no stable broad speedup is established. Chromium remains faster in the measured phases.
notes: All 21 trials are retained; no outliers were removed.
Host launch/readiness differs between guarded native and WebDriver and is excluded from speed comparisons.
Renderer controls remain CPU/offscreen. The same exact Chromium ELF was previously observed alive with software compositing/rasterization and disabled Vulkan/WebGL/WebGPU.
Intel adapter enumeration is separate; actual Lumen Intel rendering remains unverified.
Repeated workload checks are not WPT counts. This result is specific to these two source revisions and this fixed workload.
All timing trial values, ranges and matched-triplet effects are retained. These repeated workload checks are not WPT counts.
Native trials have four available memory samples and three CPU interval samples each. Chromium trials have three memory samples and two CPU interval samples each.
The separate 194/195 setter diagnostic remains a different experiment: 39.4% setter median reduction, but a slower later attribute phase and fixed-order/shared-process limitations.
